extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and USPTO patent employees (examiners, OPAP staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Ensuring compliance with the Patent Law Treaty (PLT) changes to U.S. patent prosecution procedures — especially the new minimum two-month shortened statutory reply periods (including for restriction/election of species requirements), filing-date rules, priority-restoration petitions, extension practice, and related form changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-month minimum reply period for most Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PLT provides for a time period of at least two months for replies to most Office actions and other notices; this change applies to any Office action mailed on or after December 18, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies generally to Office actions and notices; forms and OACS paragraphs were updated. Note that some pilot programs are excluded. Office actions mailed for credit after December 13, 2013 must use the updated forms. The full statutory period remains six months (see separate entry on extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-month shortened statutory period applies to Restriction/Election of Species Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For any Restriction/Election of Species Requirement mailed on or after December 18, 2013, the Examiner should indicate that the shortened statutory period for reply is set to expire two months from the mailing date of the communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Examiner inadvertently sets the former one-month period for a Restriction/Election issued on or after December 18, 2013, the applicant must file a reply within one month to avoid extension fees; the Examiner's error may be corrected by placing a formal communication on the record (e.g., an Interview Summary). Practitioners are recommended to carefully review such requirements issued on or after Dec 18, 2013 to ensure the correct period is set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full statutory period remains six months; shortened period is extendable up to additional four months
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the shortened statutory period is two months, the full statutory period for reply remains six months. The two‑month shortened period may be extended for up to an additional four months upon petition and payment of appropriate extension fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are governed by 37 CFR 1.136(a) (see also updated OACS forms). If an applicant needs additional time beyond the two-month shortened period, a petition/fee is required to obtain extensions up to the full six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Examination reply-period rule and consequence of petitioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Accelerated Examination, Office actions (other than a notice of allowance) will set a shortened statutory period for reply of at least two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are permitted for Accelerated Examination cases, but filing a petition for extension of time will result in the application being taken out of the Accelerated Examination program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date: specification (with or without claims) suffices for nonprovisional (non-design) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a nonprovisional application (other than a design) is the date on which the USPTO receives a specification, with or without claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application filed without any claims will prompt OPAP to issue a notice giving the applicant a time period to submit at least one claim to avoid abandonment. Importantly, an application will not be placed on an examiner's docket unless and until the application includes at least one claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: No drawings required for filing date (non-design) except where necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: An application (other than a design) is not required to include any drawings to be entitled to a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing that facilitates understanding of the invention — or a drawing is necessary for understanding — the USPTO will continue to require a drawing (see MPEP 608.02). Requiring drawings prior to examination should be rare and limited to situations where no examination can be performed without an illustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: No change to filing date requirements for design applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For a design patent application the filing date remains the date on which the Office receives the specification (including at least one claim) and any required drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications must still include required drawings to obtain a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in claims or drawings submitted after filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim and any drawing submitted after the filing date of an application may not contain new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-filing additions are limited to what is supported in the originally filed specification/drawings; practitioners should ensure post‑filing submissions do not introduce new subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference filing (filing by reference to a previously filed application)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application may be filed by reference (in the ADS or PLT Model International Request Form) to a previously filed application indicating that the specification and any drawings are replaced by the reference to the previously filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed by reference, OPAP will issue a notice giving the applicant a time period within which to submit an English-language copy of the specification and drawings from the previously filed application to avoid abandonment. The English-language copy will be used as the specification and drawings of the application filed by reference. As with other filings, the application will not be placed on an examiner's docket unless and until it includes a specification including at least one claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of priority rights to foreign and provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The PLT provides for restoration of the right of priority to a foreign application and restoration of the benefit of a provisional application where the delay in filing was unintentional and the application is filed within two months of the expiration of the relevant period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application may validly claim priority up to 14 months earlier (8 months for designs) if a petition to restore the right of priority/benefit (37 CFR 1.55(c) for foreign priority; 37 CFR 1.78(b) for provisional benefit) is filed and granted by the Office of Petitions. Applications claiming priority more than 12 months after the earlier filing (except as a continuing application of another nonprovisional) must include such a petition that has been granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods must be extendable by at least two months; updated OACS forms required
rubrics_metrics.description: The PLT requires that time periods for replies to most Office actions and other notices be extendable by at least two months. The USPTO modified forms and form paragraphs in OACS (current updated version cited as v3.8) for consistency with the PLT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some forms and form paragraphs were revised (e.g., PTOL‑324) to set a two‑month period where previously one month was used. These updated forms and paragraphs should be used and must be used in any Office action posted for credit after December 13, 2013. The PLT provisions expand pre-existing 1.136(a) extension practice and permit extensions in additional situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLT exceptions: certain pilot programs excluded from two-month minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain USPTO pilot programs are not encompassed by the PLT requirement and will continue to set a time period of less than two months for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples explicitly listed include the pre-appeal brief conference program and the pre-first Office action on the merits interview program. Practitioners should verify whether a given program or notice is excluded before assuming the two-month minimum applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Office-action types whose response periods changed vs. remained unchanged
rubrics_metrics.description: The memorandum reproduces a table identifying action types that were previously set with one-month response times and whether they were increased to two months or remain at one month after PLT implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed items increased to 2 months include: Mail Restriction Requirement (Restriction/Election only without rejections), Mail Notice of Informal or Non-Responsive Amendment, Mail Notice of Informal or Non-Responsive RCE Amendment, Mail Notice of Required Fees Due, Mail letter Requiring CRF (Unreadable, Non-Compliant, Not Submitted), Mail PCT Chapter I Form 206. Items that remain at 1 month include: Mail Pre-Interview Communication, Mail First Action Interview Office Action, Mail First Action without Interview (Optional FAI Step), Mail Noncompliant FAI, Mail Pre-interview First Office Action. Practitioners should consult the table to determine whether a specific notice's reply period changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner recommendation: review and remediate examiner-set reply periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners are recommended to carefully review all Restriction/Election of Species Requirements (and other affected notices) issued on or after December 18, 2013 to ensure the correct two-month shortened statutory reply period has been set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an Examiner erroneously set a one-month period for an affected notice, file the reply within one month to avoid extension fees or seek correction: the Examiner may place a formal communication on the record indicating the correct two-month period (e.g., an Interview Summary). The memorandum notes that Oliff PLC will attempt to contact Examiners if they erroneously set a one-month period.
